---
title: "Aesthetics"
---

Aesthetics decide how regions look: fill, stroke, width, opacity. You can set them
for every region at once, for a group, or for a single region, and separately for
the base, hover and selected states. This page builds that up one layer at a time.

## One look for every region

Pass a single aesthetic to `aes=`. `aes.Shape` is for filled shapes, `aes.Line` for
lines and `aes.Text` for text.

```python
from shinymap import aes, input_map

input_map("region", outline, mode="single", aes=aes.Shape(fill_color="#c7d2fe"))
```

Anything you leave out keeps the library default, including the hover and selection
styles.

## States: base, hover, select

`aes.ByState` sets a look per state. `select` and `hover` are drawn *on top of* the
base look, so they only need the properties that change.

```python
aes.ByState(
    base=aes.Shape(fill_color="#e2e8f0", stroke_color="#ffffff", stroke_width=1.5),
    hover=aes.Shape(stroke_color="#0f172a", stroke_width=2.5),
    select=aes.Shape(fill_color="#3b82f6", stroke_color="#1e40af"),
)
```

::: {layout-ncol=3}
![base](../images/generated/state-base.svg){fig-alt="Hexagon grid, all regions in the base color" width="100%"}

![hover](../images/generated/state-hover.svg){fig-alt="One hexagon outlined in dark navy" width="100%"}

![select](../images/generated/state-select.svg){fig-alt="One hexagon filled in blue" width="100%"}
:::

Set a state to `None` to switch it off, e.g. `hover=None`. Values can also be
relative to the base look: `hover=aes.Shape(stroke_width=PARENT.stroke_width + 1)`
(`from shinymap import PARENT`).

## Groups and regions: `aes.ByGroup`

`aes.ByGroup` assigns looks by key. A key can be a **region ID** or a **group name**.
Groups are defined in the outline's metadata:

```python
outline = Outline.from_dict({
    "r0": ..., "r1": ..., ...,
    "_metadata": {"groups": {"north": ["r0", ..., "r9"], "south": ["r10", ..., "r19"]}},
})

aes.ByGroup(
    north=aes.Shape(fill_color="#fde68a"),
    south=aes.Shape(fill_color="#a7f3d0"),
)
```

![](../images/generated/bygroup.svg){fig-alt="Top half of the grid yellow, bottom half green" width="50%"}

Each value can itself be an `aes.ByState`, so a group can have its own hover and
selection look.

## Which setting wins

When several entries apply to a region, the most specific one wins:

**region ID** › **group** › **type** (`__shape`, `__line`, `__text`) › **everything** (`__all`)

The same order applies to each state: base, select and hover.

A single aesthetic passed to `aes=` counts as `__all` for the element type it is
written for. Each picture below adds one more specific entry:

::: {layout-ncol=4}
![Library default](../images/generated/prec-1-wash.svg){fig-alt="All hexagons gray" width="100%"}

![`__all`](../images/generated/prec-2-all.svg){fig-alt="All hexagons lavender" width="100%"}

![+ group `north`](../images/generated/prec-3-group.svg){fig-alt="Top half yellow, bottom half lavender" width="100%"}

![+ region `r7`](../images/generated/prec-4-region.svg){fig-alt="As before, with one hexagon red" width="100%"}
:::

```python
aes.ByGroup(
    __all=aes.Shape(fill_color="#c7d2fe"),
    north=aes.Shape(fill_color="#fde68a"),
    r7=aes.Shape(fill_color="#f87171"),
)
```

## Coloring by value

`shinymap.aes.color` turns data into one color per region. Pass the result through
`aes.ByGroup`, typically from `@render_map` so the colors follow your data:

```python
from shinymap import Map, aes, output_map, render_map
from shinymap.aes.color import scale_sequential

output_map("result", outline)

@render_map
def result():
    colors = scale_sequential(counts, region_ids, max_count=5)
    return Map(aes=aes.ByGroup(**{rid: aes.Shape(fill_color=c) for rid, c in colors.items()}))
```

::: {layout-ncol=3}
![`scale_sequential`: counts](../images/generated/scale-sequential.svg){fig-alt="Hexagons in light to dark blue" width="100%"}

![`scale_diverging`: below / above a midpoint](../images/generated/scale-diverging.svg){fig-alt="Hexagons from red through gray to blue" width="100%"}

![`scale_qualitative`: categories](../images/generated/scale-qualitative.svg){fig-alt="Hexagons in blue, green and orange" width="100%"}
:::

## Where to set aesthetics

- `input_map(..., aes=...)` and `output_map(..., aes=...)` set the look when the page
  is built.
- `Map(aes=...)` returned from `@render_map` is layered on top of `output_map()`'s
  look each time it renders. Properties it does not set are kept.
- `Wash(shape=..., line=..., text=...)` replaces the library defaults for every map
  made from it (`wc.input_map`, `wc.output_map`, `wc.render_map`).
